rule: OBR fiscal year 'YYYY-YY' (6 April YYYY to 5 April YYYY+1) maps to the engine's annual period YYYY.

part_year_rule.rule: A flow parameter (a rate, threshold or amount applying to income, earnings or entitlement spread over the year) whose law changes within fiscal year Y-(Y+1) takes its day-weighted fiscal-year value in period Y, in the published world and the counterfactual alike. A point-in-time parameter (a tax charged on a transaction at the rate in force on its date) keeps the value in force on the date. A parameter whose engine file keeps statutory dates (preserve_calendar_dates) keeps them, and its formulas annualise the transactions. Where a change cannot be expressed this way, the targets it moves are flagged and excluded from that year's calibration.
part_year_rule.why: The engine's default 30 April sample keeps a mid-year change out of period Y, so calibrating period Y to the OBR's fiscal-year level would push the change's effect into the weights and contaminate every other measure that year. Day-weighting is the engine's own annualisation for flow parameters (fiscal_year_blend).
examples_verified: National Insurance primary threshold to GBP 12,570 from July 2022 (March 2022 Annex A TA.2!C7); policyengine-uk 2.130.1 stores 190 per week from 2022-04-06 and the higher amount from 6 July 2022, so its 30 April sample gives 190 for period 2022.

Universal Credit taper from 63% to 55% (October 2021 Annex A TA.2!C21, 'from 1 December 2021'); policyengine-uk 2.130.1 changes it on 2021-11-24, so its 30 April 2021 sample gives 0.63 for period 2021.

Health and Social Care Levy rates in force only for earnings paid before 6 November 2022; policyengine-uk 2.130.1's own tests say model year 2022 takes the levy rate (a change within Autumn Statement 2022's 2022-23).

reform_route.requirement: Each world's parameter values for period Y must equal the intended fiscal-year value (term 4 of the policy-world contract). Every population run records, per measure-year and world, the processed period-Y value of every changed parameter beside its intended value, and refuses a mismatch.
reform_route.policyengine_uk_2_130_1: Dated changes are written onto the statutory timeline and reprocessed with current law (policyengine_uk/utils/dated_reforms.py): use 'start.stop' range keys or parameter_changes; a bare year key sets that fiscal year only; a single-day key such as '2027-04-06' overrides one day of the annualised parameter and changes nothing for the year.
reform_route.policyengine_uk_2_125_1_and_earlier: Scenario.apply (policyengine_uk/utils/scenario.py in 2.125.1) updates the already-processed parameter tree without fiscal-year reprocessing, and annual lookups read 1 January (docs/uk_replay/YEARS.md for 2.89.2). Use the executor's date-window convention and the processed-value check.
reform_route.re_read: The evidence in this receipt must be re-read for the engine actually certified for each population before it runs.

engine_evidence.where: policyengine_uk/utils/parameters.py, convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters; called from policyengine_uk/tax_benefit_system.py on parameters.gov
engine_evidence.establishes: Annual period Y is the fiscal year starting 6 April Y. By default each government parameter is sampled at 30 April Y and that value is written over period Y, for 2015 to 2040; the 6 parameter files with fiscal_year_blend: true (CGT rates and fuel duty in 2.130.1) are day-weighted across the fiscal year; the 33 files with preserve_calendar_dates: true (including the Ofgem energy price cap and guarantee) keep statutory dates.
engine_evidence.read: 2.125.1 from its installed source; 2.130.1 from its PyPI wheel; 2026-10-15. 2.130.1 is the policyengine-uk version certified by policyengine.py#617 (with policyengine-uk-data 1.58.1); it is not yet a scorecard replay variant.

engine_evidence.establishes: The same 30 April sampling in the legacy engine; the existing replays use calendar period Y for fiscal year Y-(Y+1).

alternative_considered.rule: fiscal year Y-(Y+1) = 9/12 of period Y + 3/12 of period Y+1
alternative_considered.why_not: The engine's period Y already carries fiscal-year policy. Blending two periods would apply fiscal year Y+1's policy to January to March of fiscal year Y-(Y+1). Part-year changes are handled instead by the day-weighted fiscal-year value in period Y (part_year_rule).

limitations: Population inputs for period Y are annual projections; they are not records for 6 April to 5 April. Every comparison keeps the cy_proxies_fy divergence axis.

Cash versus liability timing (for example self-assessment receipts arriving after the year) is not bridged: cash-basis receipts are not calibration targets (policy-world contract term 2), and comparisons record the timing per head.
No part-year coverage is claimed from an annual result; the part_year_rule sets annual values, and part-year effects are recorded per measure.
A population built for these events must list every mapped period below in its certification's data_years, or the run stops with source accounting only (docs/uk_replay/HISTORICAL_ADAPTER.md).
